claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercial pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to commercial pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
Mixed principal elements produce intrinsic lattice distortions in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
The lattice distortions create a heterogeneous strain field.
The heterogeneous strain field enhances dislocation cross-slip.
The heterogeneous strain field activates multiple or additional slip systems.
Enhanced cross-slip and activation of multiple slip systems produce a more tangled and mobile dislocation network.
A tangled, mobile, and distributed dislocation network delays localized failure.
Preparing WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten under identical processing conditions will ensure a consistent baseline microstructure.
Atomic-size misfit among the multiple principal elements generates a complex field of local lattice strains in WTaTiVZr.
Pure tungsten has a more homogeneous lattice than equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Pure tungsten's homogeneous lattice results in more limited dislocation mobility and early crack initiation.
Under the specified conditions, WTaTiVZr will have a higher density of mobile dislocations than pure tungsten.
Under the specified conditions, WTaTiVZr will exhibit more frequent or pronounced cross-slip than pure tungsten.
Under the specified conditions, WTaTiVZr will exhibit more distributed slip and more active slip systems than pure tungsten.
Under the specified conditions, WTaTiVZr will show delayed crack initiation or localized failure and greater ductility and toughness than pure tungsten.
The proposed comparison isolates the effect of lattice distortions.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to testing at 1200–1400 °C and controlled strain rates representative of plasma-facing-component service.
